builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ATLAS-Bench: An Agentic Tool-Use Benchmark for Local Area Search
summary: ATLAS-Bench replaces ad hoc or anecdotal evaluation of local-search agents with 1,200 validated queries that separate mandatory requirements from preferences, plus a fixed POI knowledge base and standardized tools for measuring answer quality, trajectory quality, and execution cost. It costs integration effort against the ATLASBox environment and access to the benchmarked frontier models, since the headline results depend on GPT-6-Luna- and GLM-5.3-class systems that the reader can only reach through paid APIs. It can fail to transfer if the reader's production domain is not point-of-interest search, because the benchmark evaluates one vertical and its conclusions about model ranking may not generalize to other tool-use settings.
rationale: This is an evaluation asset rather than a deployable technique, so it is relevant only if the reader builds local-search agents, and even then it informs model selection rather than improving production performance directly.
technique: Agentic tool-use benchmark for local search

claims.statement: ATLAS-Bench replaces ad hoc or anecdotal evaluation of local-search agents with 1,200 validated queries that separate mandatory requirements from preferences, plus a fixed POI knowledge base and standardized tools for measuring answer quality, trajectory quality, and execution cost. It costs integration effort against the ATLASBox environment and access to the benchmarked frontier models, since the headline results depend on GPT-6-Luna- and GLM-5.3-class systems that the reader can only reach through paid APIs. It can fail to transfer if the reader's production domain is not point-of-interest search, because the benchmark evaluates one vertical and its conclusions about model ranking may not generalize to other tool-use settings.

Across 14 configurations of 11 models, GPT-6-Luna achieves 71.5% constraint satisfaction and 95.6% factual accuracy, while GLM-5.3 returns at least one acceptable recommendation for 85.3% of satisfiable queries versus 67.3% for GPT-6-Luna.
